'''三条家'''（'''さんじょうけ'''）は、[[藤原北家]]閑院流の嫡流にあたる[[公家]]で、家格は[[清華家]]。家紋は[[唐菱花]]を使用。[[大臣家]]の[[正親町三条家]]、[[三条西家]]を筆頭に分流も多くある。
三条家は[[藤原公実]]の二男[[藤原実行|実行]]を祖とする。京都三条の北、高倉に邸があったことから、氏の名となった。'''転法輪'''とも称し[[笛]]を家業とした。
[[幕末]]、[[明治]]に活躍した[[公卿]]の[[三条実美]]もこの一族の出である。 {{stub}}

[[幕末]]、[[明治]]に活躍した[[公卿]]の[[三条実万]]、[[三条実美]]父子はこの一族の出である。 {{stub}}

'''三条家'''（さんじょうけ、正字体：三條）は、[[藤原氏]][[藤原北家|北家]][[閑院流]]の嫡流にあたる[[公家]]で、家格は[[清華家]]。家業は笛と[[香道]]。家紋は[[唐菱花]]（三条花角、三条家花角とも言う）を使用。[[大臣家]]の[[正親町三条家]]、[[三条西家]]を筆頭に分流も多くある。
==歴史== [[閑院流]]は、[[白河天皇|白河院政]]・[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽院政]]期に上皇・天皇の外戚たる地位をほぼ独占し、院近親として絶大な権勢をふるった。[[閑院流]]の嫡流である[[藤原公実]]の二男[[藤原実行|実行]]を祖とするのが三条家である。実行は、三条の他、八条とも称したが、子の[[三条公教|公教]]、孫の[[三条実房|実房]]の嫡流が京都三条の北、高倉に邸を構えたことから、家名が定まった。
二代公教は鳥羽上皇の後見役として権勢をふるった。三代実房は「[[愚昧記]]」の著者として知られ、公事の師と仰がれていた。実房の後、嫡流は長男の[[三条公房|公房]]が継ぎ三条を称したが、三男の[[正親町三条公氏|公氏]]も三条を称したため、嫡流を'''転法輪三条'''（てんぽうりん-）、公氏の流を正親町三条と呼び区別するようになった。
戦国時代の当主[[三条公頼]]は山口の戦国大名[[大内義隆]]の元に滞在中、義隆家臣の[[陶晴賢]]の反乱に巻き込まれ、殺害されている。分家の[[三条西家]]から三条家に養子が入れられて継ぐことになった（以後、香道が三条家にも伝わる）。
江戸時代の家禄ははじめ269石余、のちに469石余。清華家として公家の中でも高い家格を誇り、大臣を多数輩出する。また代々、[[笛]]と装束の調達を家業とした。
[[幕末]]・[[明治時代]]には、[[明治維新]]の功臣[[三条実万]]・[[三条実美]]父子を輩出している。特に三条実美は、[[内閣総理大臣]]が置かれるまでの日本の首相にあたる[[右大臣]]や[[太政大臣]]の職をつとめて活躍した。
清華家は原則として華族の[[侯爵]]家に列したが、三条家は三条実美の功績を持って一段高い[[公爵]]家に列している。

==歴史== [[閑院流]]は、[[白河天皇|白河院政]]・[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽院政]]期に上皇・天皇の外戚たる地位をほぼ独占し、院近親として絶大な権勢をふるった。[[閑院流]]の嫡流である[[藤原公実]]の二男[[藤原実行|実行]]を祖とするのが三条家である。実行は、三条の他、八条とも称したが、子の[[三条公教|公教]]、孫の[[三条実房|実房]]の嫡流が京都三条の北、高倉に邸を構えたことから、家名が定まった。
二代公教は鳥羽上皇の後見役として権勢をふるった。三代実房は「[[愚昧記]]」の著者として知られ、公事の師と仰がれていた。実房の後、嫡流は長男の[[三条公房|公房]]が継ぎ三条を称したが、三男の[[正親町三条公氏|公氏]]も三条を称したため、嫡流を'''転法輪三条'''（てんぽうりん-）、公氏の流を正親町三条と呼び区別するようになった。

[[東三条家]]（[[華族]]（[[男爵]]）） }} '''三条家'''（さんじょうけ、正字体：三條）は、[[藤原氏]][[藤原北家|北家]][[閑院流]]の[[嫡流]]にあたる[[日本]]の[[氏族]]。[[公家]]・[[華族]]の家柄。公家としての家格は[[清華家]]、華族としての家格は[[公爵]]家。家業は笛と[[香道]]。家紋は[[唐菱花]]（三条花角、三条家花角とも言う）を使用。 [[明治維新]]までに三条家が輩出した[[公卿]]の数は39名。うち[[太政大臣]]まで昇った者が5名、[[左大臣]]まで昇った者が5名、[[右大臣]]まで昇った者が8名、[[内大臣]]まで昇った者が7名となっている。[[大臣家]]の[[正親町三条家]]と[[三条西家]]を筆頭に分流も多くある。 ==歴史== [[閑院流]]は、[[白河天皇|白河院政]]・[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽院政]]期に[[太上天皇|上皇]]・[[天皇]]の[[外戚]]たる地位をほぼ独占し、院近親として絶大な権勢をふるった。[[閑院流]]の[[嫡流]]である[[藤原公実]]の二男[[藤原実行|実行]]を祖とするのが三条家である。実行は、三条の他、八条とも称したが、子の[[三条公教|公教]]、孫の[[三条実房|実房]]の[[嫡流]]が京都三条の北、高倉に邸を構えたことから、家名が定まった。 二代公教は鳥羽上皇の後見役として権勢をふるった。三代実房は「[[愚昧記]]」の著者として知られ、公事の師と仰がれていた。実房の後、嫡流は長男の[[三条公房|公房]]が継ぎ三条を称したが、三男の[[正親町三条公氏|公氏]]も三条を称したため、嫡流を'''転法輪三条'''（てんぽうりん-）、公氏の流を正親町三条と呼び区別するようになった。 戦国時代の当主[[三条公頼]]は山口の戦国大名[[大内義隆]]の元に滞在中、義隆家臣の[[陶晴賢]]の反乱に巻き込まれ、殺害されている。分家の[[三条西家]]から三条家に養子が入れられて継ぐことになった（以後、[[香道]]が三条家にも伝わる）。 [[江戸時代]]の家禄ははじめ269石余、のちに469石余。[[清華家]]として公家の中でも高い家格を誇り、大臣を多数輩出する。また代々、[[笛]]と装束の調達を家業とした。 [[幕末]]・[[明治時代]]には、[[明治維新]]の功臣[[三条実万]]・[[三条実美]]父子を輩出している。特に三条実美は、[[内閣総理大臣]]が置かれるまでの日本の首相にあたる[[右大臣]]や[[太政大臣]]の職をつとめて活躍した。 [[清華家]]は原則として[[華族]]の[[侯爵]]家に列したが、三条家は[[三条実美]]の功績を持って一段高い[[公爵]]家に列している。

[[東三条家]]（[[華族]]（[[男爵]]）） }} '''三条家'''（さんじょうけ、正字体：三條）は、[[藤原氏]][[藤原北家|北家]][[閑院流]]の[[嫡流]]にあたる[[日本]]の[[氏族]]。[[公家]]・[[華族]]の家柄。公家としての家格は[[清華家]]、華族としての家格は[[公爵]]家。家業は笛と[[香道]]。家紋は[[唐菱花]]（三条花角、三条家花角とも言う）を使用。[[通字]]は『'''公'''』・『'''実'''』。'''転法輪三条家'''（てんぽうりんさんじょうけ）とも称す。 [[明治維新]]までに三条家が輩出した[[公卿]]の数は39名。うち[[太政大臣]]まで昇った者が5名、[[左大臣]]まで昇った者が5名、[[右大臣]]まで昇った者が8名、[[内大臣]]まで昇った者が7名となっている。[[大臣家]]の[[正親町三条家]]と[[三条西家]]を筆頭に分流も多くある。 __TOC__
==歴史== [[閑院流]]は、[[白河天皇|白河院政]]・[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽院政]]期に[[太上天皇|上皇]]・[[天皇]]の[[外戚]]たる地位をほぼ独占し、院近親として絶大な権勢をふるった。[[閑院流]]の[[嫡流]]である[[藤原公実]]の二男[[藤原実行|実行]]を祖とするのが三条家である。実行は、三条の他、八条とも称したが、子の[[三条公教|公教]]、孫の[[三条実房|実房]]の[[嫡流]]が京都三条の北、高倉に邸を構えたことから、家名が定まった。 二代[[三条公教|公教]]は[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽上皇]]の後見役として権勢をふるった。三代[[三条実房|実房]]は「[[愚昧記]]」の著者として知られ、公事の師と仰がれていた。実房の後、[[嫡流]]は[[長男]]の[[三条公房|公房]]が継ぎ三条を称したが、三男の[[正親町三条公氏|公氏]]も三条を称したため、嫡流を'''転法輪三条'''（てんぽうりんさんじょう）、公氏の流を正親町三条（おおぎまちさんじょう）と呼び区別するようになった。 [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]の当主[[三条公頼]]は山口の[[戦国大名]][[大内義隆]]の元に滞在中、義隆家臣の[[陶晴賢]]の反乱に巻き込まれ、殺害されている。分家の[[三条西家]]から三条家に養子が入れられて継ぐことになった（以後、[[香道]]が三条家にも伝わる）。 [[江戸時代]]の家禄ははじめ269石余、のちに469石余。[[清華家]]として公家の中でも高い家格を誇り、大臣を多数輩出する。また代々、[[笛]]と装束の調達を家業とした。 [[幕末]]・[[明治|明治時代]]には、[[明治維新]]の功臣[[三条実万]]・[[三条実美]]父子を輩出している。特に三条実美は、[[内閣総理大臣]]が置かれるまでの日本の首相にあたる[[右大臣]]や[[太政大臣]]の職をつとめて活躍した。 [[清華家]]は原則として[[華族]]の[[侯爵]]家に列したが、三条家は[[三条実美]]の功績を持って一段高い[[公爵]]家に列している。

==歴史== [[閑院流]]は、[[白河天皇|白河院政]]・[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽院政]]期に[[太上天皇|上皇]]・[[天皇]]の[[外戚]]たる地位をほぼ独占し、院近親として絶大な権勢をふるった。[[閑院流]]の[[嫡流]]である[[藤原公実]]の二男[[藤原実行|実行]]を祖とするのが三条家である。実行は、三条の他、八条とも称したが、子の[[三条公教|公教]]、孫の[[三条実房|実房]]の[[嫡流]]が京都三条の北、高倉に邸を構えたことから、家名が定まった。 二代[[三条公教|公教]]は[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽上皇]]の後見役として権勢をふるった。三代[[三条実房|実房]]は「[[愚昧記]]」の著者として知られ、公事の師と仰がれていた。実房の後、[[嫡流]]は[[長男]]の[[三条公房|公房]]が継ぎ三条を称したが、三男の[[正親町三条公氏|公氏]]も三条を称したため、嫡流を'''転法輪三条'''（てんぽうりんさんじょう）、公氏の流を正親町三条（おおぎまちさんじょう）と呼び区別するようになった。 [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]の当主[[三条公頼]]は山口の[[戦国大名]][[大内義隆]]の元に滞在中、義隆家臣の[[陶晴賢]]の反乱に巻き込まれ、殺害されている。分家の[[三条西家]]から三条家に養子が入れられて継ぐことになった（以後、[[香道]]が三条家にも伝わる）。 [[江戸時代]]の家禄ははじめ269石余、のちに469石余。[[清華家]]として公家の中でも高い家格を誇り、大臣を多数輩出する。また代々、[[笛]]と装束の調達を家業とした。 [[幕末]]・[[明治|明治時代]]には、[[明治維新]]の功臣[[三条実万]]・[[三条実美]]父子を輩出している。特に三条実美は、[[内閣総理大臣]]が置かれるまでの日本の首相にあたる[[右大臣]]や[[太政大臣]]の職をつとめて活躍した。 [[清華家]]は原則として[[華族]]の[[侯爵]]家に列したが、三条家は[[三条実美]]の功績を持って一段高い[[公爵]]家に列している。

[[東三条家]]（[[華族]]（[[男爵]]）） }} '''三条'''（さんじょう、正字体：三條）家は、[[藤原氏]][[藤原北家|北家]][[閑院流]]の[[嫡流]]にあたる[[日本]]の[[氏族]]。[[公家]]・[[華族]]の家柄。公家としての家格は[[清華家]]、華族としての家格は[[公爵]]家。家業は笛と[[香道]]。家紋は[[唐菱花]]（三条花角、三条家花角とも言う）を使用。[[通字]]は『'''公'''』・『'''実'''』。'''転法輪三条'''（てんぽうりんさんじょう）家とも称す。 [[明治維新]]までに三条家が輩出した[[公卿]]の数は39名。うち[[太政大臣]]まで昇った者が5名、[[左大臣]]まで昇った者が5名、[[右大臣]]まで昇った者が8名、[[内大臣]]まで昇った者が7名となっている。[[大臣家]]の[[正親町三条家]]と[[三条西家]]を筆頭に分流も多くある。 __TOC__
==歴史== [[閑院流]]は、[[白河天皇|白河院政]]・[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽院政]]期に[[太上天皇|上皇]]・[[天皇]]の[[外戚]]たる地位をほぼ独占し、院近親として絶大な権勢をふるった。[[閑院流]]の[[嫡流]]である[[藤原公実]]の二男[[藤原実行|実行]]を祖とするのが三条家である。実行は、三条の他、八条とも称したが、子の[[三条公教|公教]]、孫の[[三条実房|実房]]の[[嫡流]]が京都三条の北、高倉に邸を構えたことから、家名が定まった。 二代[[三条公教|公教]]は[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽上皇]]の後見役として権勢をふるった。三代[[三条実房|実房]]は「[[愚昧記]]」の著者として知られ、公事の師と仰がれていた。実房の後、[[嫡流]]は[[長男]]の[[三条公房|公房]]が継ぎ三条を称したが、三男の[[正親町三条公氏|公氏]]も三条を称したため、嫡流を'''転法輪三条'''（てんぽうりんさんじょう）、公氏の流を正親町三条（おおぎまちさんじょう）と呼び区別するようになった。 [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]の当主[[三条公頼]]は山口の[[戦国大名]][[大内義隆]]の元に滞在中、義隆家臣の[[陶晴賢]]の反乱に巻き込まれ、殺害されている。分家の[[三条西家]]から三条家に養子が入れられて継ぐことになった（以後、[[香道]]が三条家にも伝わる）。 [[江戸時代]]の家禄ははじめ269石余、のちに469石余。[[清華家]]として公家の中でも高い家格を誇り、大臣を多数輩出する。また代々、[[笛]]と装束の調達を家業とした。 [[幕末]]・[[明治|明治時代]]には、[[明治維新]]の功臣[[三条実万]]・[[三条実美]]父子を輩出している。特に三条実美は、[[内閣総理大臣]]が置かれるまでの日本の首相にあたる[[右大臣]]や[[太政大臣]]の職をつとめて活躍した。 [[清華家]]は原則として[[華族]]の[[侯爵]]家に列したが、三条家は[[三条実美]]の功績を持って一段高い[[公爵]]家に列している。

==歴史== [[閑院流]]は、[[白河天皇|白河院政]]・[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽院政]]期に[[太上天皇|上皇]]・[[天皇]]の[[外戚]]たる地位をほぼ独占し、院近親として絶大な権勢をふるった。[[閑院流]]の[[嫡流]]である[[藤原公実]]の二男[[藤原実行|実行]]を祖とするのが三条家である。実行は、三条の他、八条とも称したが、子の[[三条公教|公教]]、孫の[[三条実房|実房]]の[[嫡流]]が京都三条の北、高倉に邸を構えたことから、家名が定まった。 二代[[三条公教|公教]]は[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽上皇]]の後見役として権勢をふるった。三代[[三条実房|実房]]は「[[愚昧記]]」の著者として知られ、公事の師と仰がれていた。実房の後、[[嫡流]]は[[長男]]の[[三条公房|公房]]が継ぎ三条を称したが、三男の[[正親町三条公氏|公氏]]も三条を称したため、嫡流を'''転法輪三条'''（てんぽうりんさんじょう）、公氏の流を正親町三条（おおぎまちさんじょう）と呼び区別するようになった。 [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]の当主[[三条公頼]]は山口の[[戦国大名]][[大内義隆]]の元に滞在中、義隆家臣の[[陶晴賢]]の反乱に巻き込まれ、殺害されている。分家の[[三条西家]]から三条家に養子が入れられて継ぐことになった（以後、[[香道]]が三条家にも伝わる）。 [[江戸時代]]の家禄ははじめ269石余、のちに469石余。[[清華家]]として公家の中でも高い家格を誇り、大臣を多数輩出する。また代々、[[笛]]と装束の調達を家業とした。 [[幕末]]・[[明治|明治時代]]には、[[明治維新]]の功臣[[三条実万]]・[[三条実美]]父子を輩出している。特に三条実美は、[[内閣総理大臣]]が置かれるまでの日本の首相にあたる[[右大臣]]や[[太政大臣]]の職をつとめて活躍した。 [[清華家]]は原則として[[華族]]の[[侯爵]]家に列したが、三条家は[[三条実美]]の功績を持って一段高い[[公爵]]家に列している。

[[東三条家]]（[[華族]]（[[男爵]]）） }} '''三条'''（さんじょう、正字体：三條）家は、[[藤原氏]][[藤原北家|北家]][[閑院流]]の[[嫡流]]にあたる[[日本]]の[[氏族]]。[[公家]]・[[華族]]の家柄。公家としての家格は[[清華家]]、華族としての家格は[[公爵]]家。家業は笛と[[香道]]。家紋は[[唐菱花]]（三条花角、三条家花角とも言う）を使用。[[通字]]は『'''公'''』・『'''実'''』・『'''季'''』。'''転法輪三条'''（てんぽうりんさんじょう）家とも称す。 [[明治維新]]までに三条家が輩出した[[公卿]]の数は39名。うち[[太政大臣]]まで昇った者が5名、[[左大臣]]まで昇った者が5名、[[右大臣]]まで昇った者が8名、[[内大臣]]まで昇った者が7名となっている。[[大臣家]]の[[正親町三条家]]と[[三条西家]]を筆頭に分流も多くある。 __TOC__
==歴史== [[閑院流]]は、[[白河天皇|白河院政]]・[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽院政]]期に[[太上天皇|上皇]]・[[天皇]]の[[外戚]]たる地位をほぼ独占し、院近親として絶大な権勢をふるった。[[閑院流]]の[[嫡流]]である[[藤原公実]]の二男[[藤原実行|実行]]を祖とするのが三条家である。実行は、三条の他、八条とも称したが、子の[[三条公教|公教]]、孫の[[三条実房|実房]]の[[嫡流]]が京都三条の北、高倉に邸を構えたことから、家名が定まった。 二代[[三条公教|公教]]は[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽上皇]]の後見役として権勢をふるった。三代[[三条実房|実房]]は「[[愚昧記]]」の著者として知られ、公事の師と仰がれていた。実房の後、[[嫡流]]は[[長男]]の[[三条公房|公房]]が継ぎ三条を称したが、三男の[[正親町三条公氏|公氏]]も三条を称したため、嫡流を'''転法輪三条'''（てんぽうりんさんじょう）、公氏の流を正親町三条（おおぎまちさんじょう）と呼び区別するようになった。 [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]の当主[[三条公頼]]は山口の[[戦国大名]][[大内義隆]]の元に滞在中、義隆家臣の[[陶晴賢]]の反乱に巻き込まれ、殺害されている。分家の[[三条西家]]から三条家に養子が入れられて継ぐことになった（以後、[[香道]]が三条家にも伝わる）。 [[江戸時代]]の家禄ははじめ269石余、のちに469石余。[[清華家]]として公家の中でも高い家格を誇り、大臣を多数輩出する。また代々、[[笛]]と装束の調達を家業とした。 [[幕末]]・[[明治|明治時代]]には、[[明治維新]]の功臣[[三条実万]]・[[三条実美]]父子を輩出している。特に三条実美は、[[内閣総理大臣]]が置かれるまでの日本の首相にあたる[[右大臣]]や[[太政大臣]]の職をつとめて活躍した。 [[清華家]]は原則として[[華族]]の[[侯爵]]家に列したが、三条家は[[三条実美]]の功績を持って一段高い[[公爵]]家に列している。

{{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族}}, it held the rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. {{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族}}, it held the rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族}} ({{ill|Duke|ja|公爵}}) | origin = {{ill|Yamashiro Province|ja|山城国}}{{ill|Heian-kyō|ja|平安京}} | estate = Heian-kyō Tenpōrin Ōji

{{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族}}, it held the rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族}}, it held the rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. {{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族}}, it held the rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. {{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族}}, it held the rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. {{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家|1=Kuge}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族}}, it held the rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. {{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家|1=Kuge}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族}}, it held the rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. {{ill|Shigenoi family|ja|滋野井家}} {{small|({{ill|Baronial family|ja|羽林家}}, {{ill|Count|ja|伯爵}})}}

{{ill|Sanjō Baronial family|ja|三条男爵家}} {{small|({{ill|Baron|ja|男爵}})}}
{{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家|1=Kuge}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族}}, it held the rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. {{ill|Shigenoi family|ja|滋野井家}} {{small|({{ill|Baronial family|ja|羽林家}}, {{ill|Count|ja|伯爵}})}}

{{ill|Rokuen family|ja|鹿園家}} {{small|({{ill|Baron|ja|男爵}})}}
{{ill|Higashi-Sanjō family|ja|東三条家}} {{small|({{ill|Baron|ja|男爵}})}}
{{ill|Sanjō Baronial family|ja|三条男爵家}} {{small|({{ill|Baron|ja|男爵}})}}
{{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家|1=Kuge}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族}}, it held the rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家|12=draft}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家|12=draft}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流|12=draft}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平|12=draft}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔|12=draft}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季|12=draft}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成|12=draft}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇|12=draft}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季|12=draft}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇|12=draft}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実|12=draft}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子|12=draft}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇|12=draft}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|12=draft}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚|12=draft}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行|12=draft}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教|12=draft}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|12=draft}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第|12=draft}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家|12=draft}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家|12=draft}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. {{ill|Anekōji family|ja|姉小路家|12=draft|12=draft}} {{small|({{ill|Baronial family|ja|羽林家|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Count|ja|伯爵|12=draft|12=draft}})}}
{{ill|Rokuen family|ja|鹿園家|12=draft|12=draft}} {{small|({{ill|Baron|ja|男爵|12=draft|12=draft}})}}

{{ill|Sanjō Baronial family|ja|三条男爵家|12=draft|12=draft}} {{small|({{ill|Baron|ja|男爵|12=draft|12=draft}})}}
{{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)|12=draft|12=draft}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵|12=draft|12=draft}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏|12=draft|12=draft}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流|12=draft|12=draft}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家|1=Kuge|12=draft|12=draft}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家|12=draft|12=draft}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族|12=draft|12=draft}}, it held the Rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美|12=draft|12=draft}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|12=draft|12=draft}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|12=draft|12=draft}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家|12=draft|12=draft}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家|12=draft|12=draft}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流|12=draft|12=draft}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平|12=draft|12=draft}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔|12=draft|12=draft}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季|12=draft|12=draft}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成|12=draft|12=draft}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季|12=draft|12=draft}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実|12=draft|12=draft}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子|12=draft|12=draft}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|12=draft|12=draft}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚|12=draft|12=draft}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行|12=draft|12=draft}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教|12=draft|12=draft}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第|12=draft|12=draft}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房|12=draft|12=draft}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣|12=draft|12=draft}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記|12=draft|12=draft}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court Ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家|12=draft|12=draft}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家|12=draft|12=draft}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court Ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. {{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵|qq=draft|qq=draft}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家|1=Kuge|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it held the Rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流|qq=draft|qq=draft}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court Ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court Ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. {{ill|Higashi-Sanjō family|ja|東三条家|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{small|({{ill|Baron|ja|男爵|qq=draft|qq=draft}})}}
{{ill|Sanjō Baronial family|ja|三条男爵家|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{small|({{ill|Baron|ja|男爵|qq=draft|qq=draft}})}}
{{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵|qq=draft|qq=draft}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家|1=Kuge|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it held the Rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家|qq=draft|qq=draft}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流|qq=draft|qq=draft}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court Ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga family|ja|清華家|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources. {{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|qq=}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Samurai family|qq=}}, {{ill|Viscount|ja|子爵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Viscount|qq=}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ja|藤原氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara clan|qq=}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hokke|ja|藤原北家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara Hokke|qq=}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanin lineage|qq=}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Main lineage|qq=}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|ja|公家|1=Kuge|qq=|1=Kuge|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuge|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuge|qq=}} was {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家|1=Seiga families|2=ja|3=清華家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seiga families|qq=}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|ja|華族|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazoku|qq=}}, it held the Rank of {{ill|Duke|ja|公爵|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Duke|qq=}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karahana crest|qq=}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Sanetomi|qq=}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijō Daijin|qq=}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji Restoration|qq=}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogyū-Sanjō family|qq=}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saga family|qq=}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanin lineage|qq=}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|ja|藤原忠平|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Tadahira|qq=}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|ja|藤原師輔|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Morosuke|qq=}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnori|ja|藤原公季|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Kinnori|qq=}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Kinnari|qq=}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|ja|白河天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Shirakawa|qq=}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|qq=}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Toba|qq=}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Kinnobu|qq=}}, fathered {{ill|Empress Taiken-mon In|ja|藤原璋子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Taiken-mon In|qq=}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|ja|崇徳天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Sutoku|qq=}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Go-Shirakawa|qq=}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Emperor's maternal relatives|ja|外戚|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor's maternal relatives|qq=}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Saneyuki|qq=}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Kinari|qq=}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijō Daijin|qq=}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Takakura Palace|qq=}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Sanefusa|qq=}}, attained the position of {{ill|Sadaijin|ja|左大臣|1=Minister of the Left|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sadaijin|qq=}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gumaiki|qq=}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court Ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō Daijin|ja|太政大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daijō Daijin|qq=}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家|1=Seiga families|2=ja|3=清華家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seiga families|qq=}}, second only to the {{ill|Sekke|ja|摂家|1=Five regent houses|1=Five regent houses|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sekke|qq=}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources.
