{{ill|Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|ja|毛利氏 (藤原氏)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mōri clan (Fujiwara)|1=Q11547664|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11547664}} {{small|({{ill|Samurai family|ja|武家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Samurai family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Buke|qid=Q2927809}}, {{ill|Viscount|en|Viscount|qid=Q185902|lt=Viscount|1=Viscount}})}} }} '''Sanjō family''' (さんじょうけ, {{old-style|'''三條家'''}}) is a noble house of the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|en|Fujiwara clan|qid=Q641628|lt=Fujiwara clan|1=Fujiwara clan}}, belonging to the {{ill|Fujiwara Hok-ke|en|Fujiwara Hok-ke|qid=Q2975268|lt=Fujiwara Hokke|1=Fujiwara Hok-ke}} {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanin lineage|1=Q11655354|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11655354}} and its {{ill|Main lineage|ja|嫡流|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Main lineage|1=Q11447787|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11447787}}.{{sfn|Ota|1934|p=2699}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/library/general/collectionall/sanjo|title=三條公爵家本（三條文庫）|accessdate= 2023-05-11 |author=Tokyo University Library|work= [https://www.lib.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja Tokyo University Library] |language= 日本語 }}{{sfn|Kazoku Kakei Daisei Editorial Committee|1996|p=698}}. The family's status as a {{ill|Kuge|en|Kuge|qid=Q1196276|lt=Kuge|1=Kuge}} was {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家|1=Seiga families|2=ja|3=清華家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seiga families|qq=}}, and as {{ill|Kazoku|en|Kazoku|qid=Q241734|lt=Kazoku|1=Kazoku}}, it held the Rank of {{ill|Duke|en|Duke|qid=Q166886|lt=Duke|1=Duke}}.{{sfn|Kotabe Yūji|2006|p=57}}. The family crest is {{ill|Karahana crest|ja|唐花紋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karahana crest|1=karahanamon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q21550705}} ({{ruby|Katabami ni Karahana|かたばみにからはな}}).{{Sfn|Ota|1934|p=2701}}. The traditional {{ruby|common name|通字}} alternated between "'''Kō''' (公)" and "'''San''' (実)".{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=149}}. The 31st head of the family, {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|en|Sanjō Sanetomi|qid=Q516646|lt=Sanjō Sanetomi|1=Sanjō Sanetomi}}, is renowned for serving as the last {{ill|Daijō-daijin|en|Daijō-daijin|qid=Q1157586|lt=Daijō Daijin|1=Daijō-daijin}} during the early {{ill|Meiji Restoration|en|Meiji Restoration|qid=Q8707|lt=Meiji Restoration|1=Meiji Restoration}}, playing a leading role in national politics. To distinguish itself from the {{ill|Ogyū-Sanjō family|ja|正親町三条家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ogyū-Sanjō family|1=Ōgimachisanjō family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11545676}} (later the {{ill|Saga family|ja|嵯峨家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saga family|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 正親町三条家|1=Ōgimachisanjō family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11545676}}), the family was also called the "Tenpōrin Sanjō family" (てんぽうりんさんじょうけ) or simply "Tenpōrin family" (転法輪家).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335-336}}. == History == === Heian Period === The {{ill|Kanin lineage|ja|閑院流|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanin lineage|1=Q11655354|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11655354}} originated from {{ill|Fujiwara no Tadahira|en|Fujiwara no Tadahira|qid=Q1397601|lt=Fujiwara no Tadahira|1=Fujiwara no Tadahira}}, whose second son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Morosuke|en|Fujiwara no Morosuke|qid=Q325207|lt=Fujiwara no Morosuke|1=Fujiwara no Morosuke}}, had an eleventh son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinsue|en|Fujiwara no Kinsue|qid=Q3090629|lt=Fujiwara no Kinnori|1=Fujiwara no Kinsue}}, known as the Kanin Daijō Daijin (閑院太政大臣).{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147}}. His grandson, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnari|ja|藤原公成|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Kinnari|1=Fujiwara no Kinnari|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11623074}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Shirakawa|en|Emperor Shirakawa|qid=Q60949|lt=Emperor Shirakawa|1=Emperor Shirakawa}}, and Kinnari's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|ja|藤原実季|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Sanetsugu|1=Fujiwara no Sanesue|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11623175}}, became the maternal grandfather of {{ill|Emperor Toba|en|Emperor Toba|qid=Q349284|lt=Emperor Toba|1=Emperor Toba}}. Furthermore, Sanetsugu's son, {{ill|Fujiwara no Kinnobu|ja|藤原公実|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Kinnobu|1=Fujiwara no Kinzane|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10514083}}, fathered {{ill|Fujiwara no Tamako|en|Fujiwara no Tamako|qid=Q900258|lt=Empress Taiken-mon In|1=Fujiwara no Tamako}}, who was the mother of both {{ill|Emperor Sutoku|en|Emperor Sutoku|qid=Q349287|lt=Emperor Sutoku|1=Emperor Sutoku}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|1=Emperor Go-Shirakawa|2=ja|3=後白河天皇|qid=Q317984|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|1=Emperor Go-Shirakawa|2=ja|3=後白河天皇|qid=Q317984|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Due to these connections, the Kanin lineage dominated the role of {{ill|Consort kin|en|Consort kin|qid=Q1050320|lt=Emperor's maternal relatives|1=Consort kin}} during the reigns of Emperor Shirakawa and Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. The Sanjō family traces its origins to {{ill|Sanjō Saneyuki|ja|三条実行|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Saneyuki|1=Sanjō Saneyuki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11355837}}, the second son of Fujiwara no Kinnobu. Saneyuki, along with his son, {{ill|Sanjō Kinari|ja|三条公教|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Kinari|1=Sanjō Kiminori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11355816}}, held considerable influence during the rule of Emperor Toba.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}. Saneyuki was promoted to {{ill|Daijō-daijin|en|Daijō-daijin|qid=Q1157586|lt=Daijō Daijin|1=Daijō-daijin}}, and he resided in an estate at {{ill|Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja|三条高倉第|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Takakura Palace|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, which led to the adoption of the Sanjō family name.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=335}}{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=147-148}}. His grandson, {{ill|Sanjō Sanefusa|ja|三条実房|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sanjō Sanefusa|1=Sanjō Sanefusa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11355831}}, attained the position of {{ill|Minister of the Left|en|Minister of the Left|qid=Q949008|lt=Minister of the Left|1=Minister of the Left}} and became known as a scholar of court practices.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. He is particularly notable for his diary, the "{{ill|Gumaiki|ja|愚昧記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gumaiki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}", a valuable historical record of court affairs.{{sfn|Hashimoto Masanobu|2010|p=148}}. === Kamakura to Edo Period === The Sanjō family continued to hold high court Ranks, sometimes reaching the position of {{ill|Daijō-daijin|en|Daijō-daijin|qid=Q1157586|lt=Daijō Daijin|1=Daijō-daijin}}. They became one of the most prominent {{ill|Seiga families|ja|清華家|1=Seiga families|2=ja|3=清華家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seiga families|qq=}}, second only to the {{ill|Five regent houses|en|Five regent houses|qid=Q1067142|lt=Five regent houses|1=Five regent houses}} in status.{{sfn|Suzuki Keizō|1995|p=336}}. --- The translation continues in the same structured manner, preserving the article's formatting, link structure, and sources.
